{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean the revenue column: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Check for internal test orders: look for revenue = 999999.99 (exact match) OR with commas (e.g., 999,999.99)
# The documentation says they are 999999.99, but the string might have commas
# So we check for both representations
internal_test_exact = (sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99)
internal_test_comma = (sales['revenue'] == '999,999.99')

# Combine both conditions
internal_test_rows = internal_test_exact | internal_test_comma

# Count internal test orders
num_internal_test = internal_test_rows.sum()

# Check if any internal test orders exist in completed orders
completed_internal_test = sales[internal_test_rows & (sales['status'] == 'completed')]

# If any exist, we must exclude them from the total
if len(completed_internal_test) > 0:
    # Filter out completed internal test orders
    completed_orders_clean = sales[(sales['status'] == 'completed') & ~internal_test_rows]
    total_revenue = completed_orders_clean['revenue_clean'].sum()
else:
    # No internal test orders in completed, so just use completed orders
    completed_orders_clean = sales[sales['status'] == 'completed']
    total_revenue = completed_orders_clean['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Print results
print(f"Number of internal test orders (exact 999999.99): {internal_test_exact.sum()}")
print(f"Number of internal test orders (with commas '999,999.99'): {internal_test_comma.sum()}")
print(f"Total internal test orders found: {num_internal_test}")
print(f"Completed internal test orders found: {len(completed_internal_test)}")
print(f"Total revenue from completed orders (excluding internal test): {total_revenue}")"}
